newsitem.title: UK: British E coli outbreaks claims 11th victim.
newsitem.headline: British E coli outbreaks claims 11th victim.

text.p: A food poisoning outbreak in Scotland, caused by the E coli bacteria, has claimed its 11th victim, hospital officials said on Wednesday.
The latest to die was a 70-year-old man who was being treated in a Glasgow hospital.
The poisoning first broke out among pensioners who attended a lunch and was traced to meat pies supplied by an award-winning Scottish butcher's shop.
A second butcher's shop has now been closed after it was linked to one of the sufferers.
Officials say there are now more than 200 confirmed cases of E coli poisoning, making it the worst such outbreak in Britain.
E coli is a common gut bacteria that is normally harmless, but a toxic strain that lives in cattle can be passed to humans via manure or improper slaughtering.
All of those killed by the food poisoning have been elderly. Several children have been treated for kidney failure.
Recent outbreaks of E coli poisoning have been reported in the United States and Japan.
